title: The Double Asset
premise: Petra Fairweather, a deniable fixer for an embassy that exists on no map, discovers the safe house where 'the incident' happened has been listed for sale — and the listing photos show details only someone who was inside could know. Following the listing leads him through three governments' buried files to a twin brother he never knew he had, whose identity Petra has unknowingly been living for a decade. As an assassin closes in ahead of the Frankfurt market open — when a forged inheritance will either clear or detonate — Petra must decide whether to expose the truth or bury it deeper. He chooses exposure, trading his own invisibility for his brother's name, and walks out of the shadows into daylight, finally able to sleep.
about_author: Jonah Okonkwo is a former logistics coordinator for humanitarian missions who writes thrillers about the paperwork behind the world's secrets. He lives between Lagos and Lisbon and claims every plot in his books is at least forty percent true.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Scrolling property listings at 3 a.m., he finds the safe house for sale — and in photo seven, a coffee cup he remembers holding the night of the incident. The emotional beat: cold recognition that his carefully erased life has been catalogued by a stranger.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Address
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He pulls the deed history and finds the house registered under a name that makes his hands shake: Fairweather — his own, but with a birthdate eleven months off his. Emotional beat: vertigo as the self he built begins to look borrowed.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, intercut with the assassin Ilse's. Petra calls the listing agent and reaches a man with his exact voice. Meanwhile Ilse receives her contract: eliminate the asset before Frankfurt opens. Emotional beat: dread doubling into something like hope.

chapters.title: Twin
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In a border-town archive he learns of Elias, the brother taken by their father's handlers while Petra was raised abroad as cover. The incident wasn't his failure — it was Elias's operation wearing his face. Emotional beat: grief for a stolen decade.

chapters.title: Ilse's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. We see her methodical preparation and her own buried grievance: she once was an asset listed for sale herself. Emotional beat: unsettling sympathy; the hunter has a conscience, which makes her more dangerous, not less.

chapters.title: The Open House
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He attends the open house as a buyer and meets Elias in the kitchen where everything happened. Elias denies everything too smoothly; Petra realizes one of them is lying about which twin survived the incident. Emotional beat: mirror-stage horror.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Countdown
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. With markets opening in thirty-six hours, Petra races to extract the inheritance file from a bank vault requiring biometric proof — proof both twins can provide. Ilse is ordered to kill whichever twin shows up. Emotional beat: ticking-clock panic sharpened by betrayal.

chapters.title: The Vault
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Inside the vault he finds not money but recordings: their father's confession that the twins were always one asset split in two, and that 'the incident' was staged to test which half would break. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: Before the Bell
chapters.summary: Climax. All POVs converge at the exchange plaza. Petra broadcasts the confession to three governments simultaneously, forcing them to disown the asset rather than silence two witnesses. Ilse, given the shot, lowers her rifle and walks away. Emotional beat: cathartic exposure over safe silence.

chapters.title: Daylight
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, weeks later. The embassy never existed, so it cannot retaliate; the brothers divide the inheritance and the truth. Petra buys the safe house under his real name and sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
